science.title: Avian influenza amplified age-related mortality in a long-lived seabird
science.description: In recent years, highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have caused mass mortality events in seabirds worldwide, raising concern for long-lived species with low reproductive rates. Using 28 years of ringing data together with individual-level data from the 2022 mass mortality event in northwestern European Sandwich terns (Thalasseus sandvicensis), we show that mortality was biased towards older individuals, while no sex bias was observed. HPAI-related mortality increased from approximately 5–10% in young breeders to more than 40% in the oldest individuals. This age-biased loss likely removed the most experienced individuals from the population. Our findings highlight a previously underappreciated mechanism through which HPAI outbreaks may impair the resilience of long-lived avian populations. In this study, the authors show that during the 2022 avian influenza outbreak, Sandwich tern mortality rose sharply with age: over 40% of the oldest birds died versus 5–10% of young breeders, likely removing experienced individuals and potentially weakening population resilience.

science.title: A pyridoxal phosphate-dependent enzyme platform for stereoselective synthesis of γ-tertiary-nitro-noncanonical amino acids
science.description: Non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs) are privileged building blocks for the synthesis of natural products, biocatalysts, and drug molecules. Among them, γ-tertiary-nitro-α-amino acids are highly valuable yet remain scarcely explored due to challenges in synthetic accessibility. Although pyridoxal-5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzymes are powerful biocatalysts for ncAA production, no enzymatic platform has, to the best of our knowledge, enabled efficient access to γ-tertiary-nitro-α-amino acids. Here, we report a PLP-dependent enzymatic platform that selectively couples O-acetyl-serine with secondary nitroalkanes to yield γ-tertiary-nitro-α-amino acids. Through reaction design, enzyme screening, and directed evolution, we repurpose SidM, an enzyme that catalyzes pyrrole ring formation in the siderochelin biosynthetic pathway, into a highly active and stereoselective biocatalyst, affording γ-tertiary-nitro-α-amino acids in up to 99% yield and 99% diastereomeric excess. This enzyme exhibits broad substrate scope and good evolvability, allowing enhancement of catalytic efficiency or inversion of diastereoselectivity at the Cγ nitro center, and is readily scalable to gram synthesis. Mechanistic analyses combining computation and mutagenesis elucidate the structural determinants of activity and stereocontrol. This work establishes a general, tunable and scalable biocatalytic platform for the synthesis of γ-tertiary-nitro-α-amino acids, expanding the synthetic repertoire of PLP-dependent enzymes for asymmetric C–C bond formation. γ-Tertiary-nitro-α-amino acids are valuable non-canonical amino acids that remain scarcely explored due to challenges in synthetic accessibility. Here, the authors report a pyridoxal-5′-phosphate (PLP)- dependent enzymatic platform that selectively couples O-acetyl-serine and secondary nitroalkanes to yield γ-tertiary-nitro-α-amino acids.

science.title: Effects of new pictorial cigarette pack warnings on Vietnamese smokers’ perceptions and smoking behaviors: a single-factor, between-subjects experimental study
science.description: This study aimed to assess the effects of different cigarette package pictorial health warnings (PHW) configurations that Vietnam might consider in the future. A 5-arm randomized experiment was conducted with 1,010 adult smokers in Vietnam in 2024. We measured four sets of outcomes: (1) emotional and cognitive responses, (2) attitudes and beliefs about smoking-related harms, and (3) behavioral intentions measured immediately after viewing PHWs; and (4) recall and behavioral outcomes at two-week follow-up. Group 2 (new PHWs, covering 85%) had significantly higher negative emotional responses than group 4 (new PHWs + Quitline + Plain packaging, covering 85%). For ‘smoking causes oral cancer’ and ‘smoking causes bleeding in the brain and stroke’, the mean belief scores of group 2 (new PHWs, covering 85%) were significantly higher than those of the control group. At two-week follow-up, participants in group 3 (new PHWs + Quitline, covering 85%) and group 4 (new PHWs + Quitline + plain packaging, covering 85%) were more likely to recall the quitline number compared to the control group. Additionally, participants in group 4 (new PHWs + Quitline + plain packaging, covering 85%) had higher odds of forgoing a cigarette at two-week follow-up compared to the control group. No significant impact of groups on quit intention or cessation behaviors was observed. Our study supports refreshing PHWs, showing that new PHWs with quitline enhanced awareness of quitline services. Plain packaging with new PHWs increased the likelihood of forgoing cigarettes, a precursor to cessation attempts. Trial registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06818786, 24/08/2024).
